fruits.extendedStory: The story goes that a future king once slept outside it. Gustav Vasa, later King of Sweden, had slipped out of captivity in Denmark in farmer's clothes, the tale says. He reached Lübeck after the gate had shut, and is said to have slept out here with the ox-drivers. Lübeck's council then refused to hand him over, it is said. The gate had room for 30 guns, yet none of them ever fired a shot. After long arguments over tearing it down, the citizens voted in 1863 to keep it, by just one vote.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Sage nach schlief hier einmal ein künftiger König vor dem Tor. Gustav Vasa, später König von Schweden, war in Bauernkleidern aus der Gefangenschaft in Dänemark entkommen, so erzählt man. Er kam erst, als das Tor schon geschlossen war, und soll die Nacht mit den Ochsentreibern hier draußen verbracht haben. Der Rat soll sich dann geweigert haben, ihn auszuliefern. Im Tor war Platz für 30 Geschütze, doch aus ihnen wurde nie ein Schuss abgefeuert. Jahrelang stritt man über den Abriss, bis die Bürgerschaft 1863 mit nur einer Stimme Mehrheit beschloss, es zu erhalten.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The story goes that a future king once slept outside it. Gustav Vasa, later King of Sweden, had slipped out of captivity in Denmark in farmer's clothes, the tale says. He reached Lübeck after the gate had shut, and is said to have slept out here with the ox-drivers. Lübeck's council then refused to hand him over, it is said. The gate had room for 30 guns, yet none of them ever fired a shot. After long arguments over tearing it down, the citizens voted in 1863 to keep it, by just one vote.

localizedStory.de: Schau genau hin: Das Holstentor steht schief. Sein Südturm sackte in den weichen Boden, wohl schon, als das Tor noch gebaut wurde.
localizedStory.en: Look closely: the Holstentor leans. Its south tower began sinking into the soft ground, probably while the gate was still being built.

fruits.name: Holstentor
fruits.story: Look closely: the Holstentor leans. Its south tower began sinking into the soft ground, probably while the gate was still being built.

fruits.extendedStory: Painters and photographers took to this spot in the twentieth century for its view of the Old Town. That is how it got its nickname, Painters' Corner. Across the water, river boats once moored with salt from Lüneburg, so that bank was called the salt market. The street at the far end of the wooden bridge is named after a man called Dankwart. Which Dankwart he was, and why the street got his name, nobody knows.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Im zwanzigsten Jahrhundert entdeckten Maler und Fotografen diesen Ort für sich, wegen seines Blicks auf die Altstadt. So kam er zu seinem Spitznamen, Malerwinkel. Drüben am Ufer machten einst die Flussschiffe mit dem Salz aus Lüneburg fest, darum hieß es Salzmarkt. Die Straße am anderen Ende der hölzernen Brücke trägt den Namen eines Dankwart. Welcher Dankwart das war und was er mit der Straße zu tun hatte, weiß niemand.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Painters and photographers took to this spot in the twentieth century for its view of the Old Town. That is how it got its nickname, Painters' Corner. Across the water, river boats once moored with salt from Lüneburg, so that bank was called the salt market. The street at the far end of the wooden bridge is named after a man called Dankwart. Which Dankwart he was, and why the street got his name, nobody knows.

localizedStory.de: Von hier aus scheinen die Doppeltürme der Marienkirche westlich vom Turm der Petrikirche zu stehen. Dabei stehen sie einen Block weiter östlich.
localizedStory.en: From here, the twin towers of St. Marien seem to stand west of St. Petri's tower. Really, they are a block further east.

fruits.name: Malerwinkel
fruits.story: From here, the twin towers of St. Marien seem to stand west of St. Petri's tower. Really, they are a block further east.

fruits.extendedStory: The mouse comes from a warning tale. Lübeck would stay free, the story goes, as long as a great rose tree here kept blooming. One morning, the tale goes on, it had wilted, because a mouse's young had gnawed through its root. Soon after, it is said, the town had to give in to the Danes. Once Lübeck was free again, the council had the tree and the mouse carved in stone, so the legend says. It was meant, the tale says, as a sign that small troubles can grow into a big misfortune overnight.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Maus stammt aus einer Warnsage. Der Sage nach blieb Lübeck frei, solange hier ein großer Rosenbaum blühte. Eines Morgens war er verwelkt, so erzählt man, denn die Jungen einer Maus hatten seine Wurzel durchgenagt. Bald darauf, heißt es, musste sich die Stadt den Dänen ergeben. Als Lübeck wieder frei war, ließ der Rat Baum und Maus in Stein hauen, so die Geschichte. Das Bild sollte, heißt es, zeigen, dass aus kleinen Übeln über Nacht ein großes Unglück werden kann.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The mouse comes from a warning tale. Lübeck would stay free, the story goes, as long as a great rose tree here kept blooming. One morning, the tale goes on, it had wilted, because a mouse's young had gnawed through its root. Soon after, it is said, the town had to give in to the Danes. Once Lübeck was free again, the council had the tree and the mouse carved in stone, so the legend says. It was meant, the tale says, as a sign that small troubles can grow into a big misfortune overnight.

localizedStory.de: Such die kleine Kirchenmaus aus Stein. Wer sie berührt, soll Glück haben, sagt man. Darum ist sie schon ganz dunkel geworden.
localizedStory.en: Find the little church mouse carved in stone. People say touching it brings luck, and that is why it has been rubbed so dark.

fruits.name: St.-Marien-Kirche
fruits.story: Find the little church mouse carved in stone. People say touching it brings luck, and that is why it has been rubbed so dark.

fruits.extendedStory: The legend begins with Charlemagne, who spared that same stag four hundred years earlier and hung a golden collar on it. The spring was never quite tamed, the tale says. If you listen, they say you can still hear it rushing deep below, and that is why the towers are crooked. Two old paintings inside tell the legend. And on one of the old chapels, look for a little marble angel blowing soap bubbles.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Sage beginnt vierhundert Jahre früher bei Karl dem Großen: Er verschonte denselben Hirsch und hängte ihm ein goldenes Halsband um. Die Quelle ließ sich nie ganz bändigen, so erzählt man. Wer genau hinhört, soll sie noch tief unten rauschen hören, und darum, heißt es, sind die Türme schief. Zwei alte Gemälde im Dom erzählen die Sage. Und such auf einer der alten Kapellen den kleinen Marmorengel: Er bläst Seifenblasen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The legend begins with Charlemagne, who spared that same stag four hundred years earlier and hung a golden collar on it. The spring was never quite tamed, the tale says. If you listen, they say you can still hear it rushing deep below, and that is why the towers are crooked. Two old paintings inside tell the legend. And on one of the old chapels, look for a little marble angel blowing soap bubbles.

localizedStory.de: Der Sage nach gründete Heinrich der Löwe den Dom dort, wo ein Hirsch mit goldenem Kreuz im Geweih an eine Quelle kam.
localizedStory.en: Legend says Henry the Lion founded the Dom where a stag came to a spring, with a golden cross between its antlers.

fruits.name: Dom
fruits.story: Legend says Henry the Lion founded the Dom where a stag came to a spring, with a golden cross between its antlers.

fruits.extendedStory: A local legend says marzipan was invented in Lübeck in 1407. After a famine, the tale goes, the city had nothing left but sugar and almonds. So, it is said, people made a kind of bread from them. Königsberg tells the very same story, set two years later. The firm goes back to Johann Georg Niederegger, a confectioner from Ulm. He took over a Lübeck sweet shop in 1806.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Einer Legende nach wurde Marzipan 1407 in Lübeck erfunden. Nach einer Hungersnot, so erzählt man, gab es in der Stadt nur noch Zucker und Mandeln. Daraus soll man eine Art Brot gemacht haben. Königsberg erzählt genau dieselbe Geschichte, nur zwei Jahre später. Die Firma geht auf Johann Georg Niederegger zurück, einen Konditor aus Ulm. Er übernahm 1806 eine Lübecker Konditorei.
localizedExtendedStory.en: A local legend says marzipan was invented in Lübeck in 1407. After a famine, the tale goes, the city had nothing left but sugar and almonds. So, it is said, people made a kind of bread from them. Königsberg tells the very same story, set two years later. The firm goes back to Johann Georg Niederegger, a confectioner from Ulm. He took over a Lübeck sweet shop in 1806.

localizedStory.de: Such oben nach zwölf lebensgroßen Menschen aus Marzipan, vom Schriftsteller Thomas Mann bis zum Modeschöpfer Wolfgang Joop.
localizedStory.en: Upstairs, look for twelve life-size people made of marzipan, from the writer Thomas Mann to the fashion designer Wolfgang Joop.

fruits.name: Niederegger
fruits.story: Upstairs, look for twelve life-size people made of marzipan, from the writer Thomas Mann to the fashion designer Wolfgang Joop.

fruits.extendedStory: Lübeckers have a nickname for these rooms: Kabäusterchen. The story goes that the founder was a poor boy whose master called him Morgenweg, or away tomorrow. When asked when he would go out into the world, the tale says, he always answered that he would leave tomorrow. One day he sailed off, it is said, came home rich and, as a councillor, founded this hospital. In truth, rich citizens gave it, and it was finished in 1286. Part of it is still a home for old people today.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Lübecker haben für diese Kammern einen Spitznamen: Kabäusterchen. Der Sage nach war der Gründer ein armer Junge. Fragte man ihn, wann er in die Welt hinausziehe, sagte er stets, morgen wolle er weg. Darum nannte ihn sein Herr Morgenweg, erzählt man. Eines Tages segelte er davon, heißt es, kam reich zurück und gründete als Ratsherr dieses Hospital. Gestiftet haben es in Wahrheit reiche Bürger, und 1286 war es fertig. Ein Teil ist bis heute ein Alten- und Pflegeheim.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Lübeckers have a nickname for these rooms: Kabäusterchen. The story goes that the founder was a poor boy whose master called him Morgenweg, or away tomorrow. When asked when he would go out into the world, the tale says, he always answered that he would leave tomorrow. One day he sailed off, it is said, came home rich and, as a councillor, founded this hospital. In truth, rich citizens gave it, and it was finished in 1286. Part of it is still a home for old people today.

localizedStory.de: In der großen Halle stehen winzige Holzkammern, oben offen. An den Türen stehen noch Namen und Nummern der alten Menschen, die darin wohnten.
localizedStory.en: Tiny wooden rooms, open at the top, stand in the great hall. Their doors still show the names of the old people who lived there.

fruits.name: Heiligen-Geist-Hospital
fruits.story: Tiny wooden rooms, open at the top, stand in the great hall. Their doors still show the names of the old people who lived there.

fruits.extendedStory: The sculptor simply mixed the two up when he made it in 1907. A former pupil of the school here, an industrialist named Ramm, paid for the fountain. It stands in the yard of the Johanneum, the school named after that convent. The convent was Lübeck's first, because until it was founded, the town had none at all. The old dining hall is the part of it that survived.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Bildhauer hat die beiden 1907 schlicht verwechselt. Bezahlt hat den Brunnen ein ehemaliger Schüler der Schule hier, der Industrielle Ramm. Er steht auf dem Hof des Johanneums, das seinen Namen von jenem Kloster hat. Es war das erste Kloster Lübecks, denn bis dahin hatte die Stadt gar keines. Erhalten ist davon nur der alte Speisesaal.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The sculptor simply mixed the two up when he made it in 1907. A former pupil of the school here, an industrialist named Ramm, paid for the fountain. It stands in the yard of the Johanneum, the school named after that convent. The convent was Lübeck's first, because until it was founded, the town had none at all. The old dining hall is the part of it that survived.

localizedStory.de: Falscher Johannes! Der Brunnen zeigt Johannes den Täufer. Das Kloster, das hier einst stand, war aber einem anderen Johannes geweiht, dem Evangelisten.
localizedStory.en: Wrong John! The fountain shows John the Baptist, but the convent that once stood here was dedicated to another John, the Evangelist.

fruits.name: Johannis-der-Täufer-Brunnen
fruits.story: Wrong John! The fountain shows John the Baptist, but the convent that once stood here was dedicated to another John, the Evangelist.

fruits.extendedStory: Unmarried daughters of Lübeck merchants once lived here, in a convent founded for them. Today its rooms hold a museum with 28 altarpieces. The crown of them all is Hans Memling's Passion altarpiece, the most famous work of art in Lübeck. A merchant family, the Greverades, gave it in 1491, but not to the convent. They gave it to the Dom.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Hier lebten einst die unverheirateten Töchter Lübecker Kaufleute, in einem Kloster, das eigens für sie gegründet wurde. Heute zeigen seine Räume ein Museum mit 28 Altären. Die Krönung ist das Passionsretabel von Hans Memling, das berühmteste Kunstwerk Lübecks. Die Kaufmannsfamilie Greverade stiftete es 1491, aber nicht dem Kloster. Sie stiftete es dem Dom.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Unmarried daughters of Lübeck merchants once lived here, in a convent founded for them. Today its rooms hold a museum with 28 altarpieces. The crown of them all is Hans Memling's Passion altarpiece, the most famous work of art in Lübeck. A merchant family, the Greverades, gave it in 1491, but not to the convent. localizedStory.de: Der Sage nach wuchs die hohe, gerade Klostermauer ganz ohne Gerüst von außen. Ein Meister aus Braunschweig baute sie mit fünf Gesellen.
localizedStory.en: Legend says the convent's high, straight wall rose with no outside scaffolding, built by a Braunschweig master and five journeymen.

fruits.name: Museumsquartier Sankt Annen
fruits.story: Legend says the convent's high, straight wall rose with no outside scaffolding, built by a Braunschweig master and five journeymen.
